inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The p. 84 signal-transduction map: glucagon (liver) and epinephrine (liver and muscle, β receptor) → GPCR → adenylate cyclase (ATP → cAMP) → protein kinase A → phosphorylase kinase ON → glycogen phosphorylase ON, synthase OFF; epinephrine (liver, α₁ receptor) → endoplasmic reticulum → calcium; calcium-calmodulin in muscle during contraction; insulin (liver and muscle) → tyrosine kinase dimer receptor → protein phosphatase → synthase ON, phosphorylase kinase OFF.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: Glycogen synthesis and degradation map with numbered enzymes
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The p. 84 glycogen map: glycolysis/gluconeogenesis boxes on glucose; glucose-6-P ↔ glucose-1-P → UDP-glucose → glycogen (glycogenesis: ②③④ with the branching enzyme building α-(1,6) branches); glycogenolysis: ⑤ phosphorylase releasing glucose-1-P to the limit dextrin, ⑥⑦ the debranching enzyme's transferase and glucosidase, the lysosome-only ⑧ arm to glucose; red Roman numerals I-V marking the five storage-disease blocks with the side lists (disease type / glycogen enzymes).

inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The p. 85 GSD table (DISEASE / FINDINGS / DEFICIENT ENZYME / COMMENTS) covering von Gierke I, Pompe II, Cori III, Andersen IV, McArdle V with full findings, enzymes, and comments.

notes: Both p. 84 figures are full redraws: sv1 the hormonal signal-transduction map (fasted glucagon/epinephrine cAMP-PKA cascade with the α₁-calcium arm and insulin's phosphatase arm, laid out as fasted/fed panels over a shared enzyme cascade), sv2 the numbered glycogenesis/glycogenolysis map with the five Roman-numeral disease blocks and both side lists. sv3, the p. 85 storage-disease table, is implemented as the note's verbatim-contract table block per the G3/E10 note-block pattern.
